ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-inclusion and continuous screening of all general partners, limited partners, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, FATF Public Statements, Luxembourg Ministry of Finance sanctions list, INTERPOL Red Notices, and high-quality PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, family member, or close associate. Re-screening must occur at least every 90 days and all screening evidence must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via eJustice.lu and lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be distinguishable from existing RCS entries and must end with 'Société en commandite spéciale' or 'SCSp'. Names may be submitted in French, German, Luxembourgish, English, or other Latin-script languages; non-Latin scripts require a certified transliteration into the Latin alphabet. The name must not be contrary to Luxembourg public policy or misleading as to the entity's corporate form or regulated activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Avocat / Law Firm / Cabinet d'avocat / Barreau
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce / Arbitration Court
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 90 days upon written request to LBR and payment of the statutory fee before expiry. If LBR rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration request via eJustice within 10 business days. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may lodge a judicial appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within one month of notification. In parallel, a fresh reservation application with alternative names should be filed to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a passive SCSp holding vehicle, a virtual office is permissible provided a Luxembourg-registered domiciliation agent maintains a physical Luxembourg address and accepts service of process. For the underlying licensed cross-border commercial litigation activity and any client-funds account, a purely virtual office is not permissible: a physical Luxembourg office with client confidentiality, file storage, and professional substance is required under legal-profession and AML/CFT rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15% annual risk for the passive SCSp structure and approximately 30% annual risk for the licensed litigation operating entity; probability increases to 50% if client funds or an IOLTA-analogue trust account are held at the Luxembourg address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 101-103 as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013 on the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp), read with the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers (Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés) and the Grand-Ducal Regulation governing electronic filing and publication in the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by the Ministry of Justice via the eJustification online portal; publication official gazette: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Deed of Constitution) executed before a Luxembourg notary or by private deed, followed by mandatory registration filing with the RCS and statutory publication in the RESA under the amended Law of 19 December 2002.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital is required for an SCSp; the partnership deed freely determines capital and contribution obligations in cash or in kind. No escrow account rule applies to partnership capital. Contributions are recorded in the subscription schedule; statutory audit and filing obligations may arise only if the SCSp exceeds large-enterprise thresholds under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the organizers and founding partners of the Partnership as follows: 1. The deed of constitution constituting the Partnership as a société en commandite spéciale under Luxembourg law is hereby approved and adopted in final form. 2. The partners listed in the subscription schedule are admitted, and their capital contribution obligations are accepted. 3. The registered office of the Partnership is fixed at the address stated in the deed, within the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 4. [General Partner Name] is hereby appointed general partner, and [Manager Name] is appointed day-to-day manager, each with authority to file the statutory instrument before the Luxembourg Business Registers and to open trust accounting bank facilities. 5. All pre-incorporation acts of the organizers are ratified in full.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Verification and Availability Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - eJustification portal / official business names database search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the eJustification portal or the public RCS database (lbr.lu) and conduct a prior art search for the desired firm name, including the mandatory legal form suffix 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or 'SCSp'. Verify that the name does not conflict with protected names, trademarks, or registered entities. The partners must certify the chosen name in the draft deed; the notary will formally check legality at signing.
required_dossiers: Requested corporate name variants
Proof of ownership/authorization for any name containing a personal surname
Certificate of no earlier similar RCS registration (downloadable verification report)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS or the notary flags a conflict or misleading name, the partners submit a rectification certificate renaming the entity; no fee refund is granted, but a fresh name check can be expedited via the eJustification support desk within one business day. A formal refusal can be appealed before the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) sitting in commercial matters per Article 18 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Deed of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire luxembourgeois) or attorneys drafting a private deed; Ministry of Justice for legalization if signed abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the deed of constitution containing all mandatory particulars: legal form SCSp, duration, registered office address, corporate object, appointment of general partner and manager, subscription schedule, and conditions precedent. The deed may be executed as a notarial act or by private signing. The notary will collect the signature pages, verify identity and legal capacity of each partner, and issue protocolized copies. Apostille or consular legalization is required if any signature occurs outside the Grand Duchy.
required_dossiers: Draft deed of constitution (acte constitutif)
Valid passport or national identity card of each partner
Proof of residential/professional address of each partner and the general partner
Certificate of good standing (attestation de non-condamnation) for natural persons acting as manager
Notarized power of attorney if represented
Foreign corporate partner: certificate of tax residence and directors' resolution authorizing admission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary or the Ministry of Justice query the deed, the parties file a corrective rider (addendum) or a restated deed within 15 days; if the manager’s certificate of non-condemnation is missing, the appointment condition is treated as unmet and a substitute manager is named by ordinary majority of the partners. No appeal is available against a notary's refusal; the deed is simply redrafted and resubmitted to a different notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing and Legal Entity Number Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via the eJustification single-window electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed deed electronically on the eJustification platform, annexing the mandatory RCS registration form (formulaire modulaire F1), the text of the articles, the appointment certificates, and the treasurer's declaration confirming receipt of initial contributions. The RCS will assign the Legal Entity Number (Numéro d'immatriculation) and issue the certificate of registration. Registration fees of approximately EUR 24 are payable electronically. The general partner must sign the filing request; if the general partner is a corporate vehicle, its board resolution and legal existence proof are annexed.
required_dossiers: Signed deed of constitution
RCS registration form (Formular F1 or notary-signed module)
Proof of registered office address (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Acceptance of appointment by general partner and manager
Certificate of lawful use of registered office premises
Treasurer's certificate on contributions received (if functions in kind or cash)
Bank account details for fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for rectification (demande de régularisation), cure the defect by resubmitting the corrected form within one month of the notification; failure to cure leads to refusal. The applicant may appeal the refusal before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months. Practical remedy: expedited refiling via a notary's authenticated electronic channel with a preliminary pre-check by an RCS helpdesk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Publication in the RESA Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice - RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) publishing service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically transmits the filing particulars to the RESA. The general partner must verify that the RESA publication contains the exact legal form (SCSp), the registered office, the corporate object, the identity of the general partners and authorized managers, and the capital subscription data. The RESA publication is constitutive of third-party opposability as from the date of edition; the partnership cannot invoke the deed of constitution against third parties before publication under Article 2 of the Law of 19 December 2002.
required_dossiers: RCS registration notice generated automatically
Proof of RCS registration number
RESA publication fee confirmation (EUR 19, included in registration if prepaid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice contains material errors, the general partner files a rectification request with the RCS, which will republish a corrected notice within the next publication cycle; third parties acting in reliance on the erroneous text before rectification remain protected unless they knew of the error. Corrective publication has retroactive effect only from the date of the original filing where no third-party reliance has intervened.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Attainment of Registered Physical Office and Domiciliation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) verification unit; municipal administration of the commune where the office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is physically located in Luxembourg and suitable for receiving service of process. Where the SCSp is formed by a corporate service provider, execute a standard domiciliation agreement with a licensed domiciliation agent registered under the Law of 31 May 1999. Verify that the lease or domiciliation agreement expressly allows professional registered office use, and obtain the landlord's or domiciliary agent's consent letter for RCS purposes. The RCS may conduct occasional on-site verification of the office's material existence.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease agreement for the office premises
Domestication/domiciliation agreement with an authorized corporate service provider
Landlord's written consent to registration as registered office
Building compliance certificate (certificat de conformité) if newly constructed
Extract from the municipal cadastre showing permitted administrative use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or RCS rejects the premises as unsuitable (e.g., purely residential), the partners execute a new domiciliation agreement with a licensed provider within 30 days and file a registered office change; failure to maintain a permitted office subjects the SCSp to dissolution by the registry after a formal injunction. A challenge can be brought before the administrative courts within three months of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, AML, Social Security, and IOLTA Trust Account Configuration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Luxembourg Bar Association (Barreau de Luxembourg); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); anti-money laundering supervision via the CSSF where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the mandatory registration with the AEDT for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net worth tax, and VAT where an economic activity is carried out. Register for Luxembourg social security with the CCSS if the SCSp has employees. For ISIC 6910 cross-border litigation chambers, obtain or verify the partners' admission to the Luxembourg Bar (licensed avocats) and comply with AML/CFT law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended). Open the dedicated IOLTA trust account with a Luxembourg credit institution and execute the equivalent of an original client-money agreement, ensuring the trust ledger is separate from the SCSp's own cash account.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of incorporation
Board resolution authorizing opening of bank accounts
Tax registration forms (Formulaire 850 returned to AEDT)
VAT threshold declaration if applicable
Bar registration certificate for each managing avocat
AML compliance manual and beneficial ownership declaration
IOLTA trust deed and bank mandate
Social security form for any employees (CSSF registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT or CCSS queries the registrations, correct the file through the business-filing platform or by written reply within the prescribed deadline (15 days). A refusal of VAT or tax registration may be appealed to the Director of the Administration within 3 months and subsequently to the Administrative Tribunal. Bar admission refusals are challengeable under Article 35 of the Law of 10 August 1991; bank account refusal is cure by selection of a second credit institution. Continuous AML inspection deficiencies are remedied by filing a rectification plan with the Bar's AML compliance department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Justice - Department for Regulated Professionals, jointly with the Luxembourg Bar Association (Barreau de Luxembourg / Ordre des Avocats du Barreau de Luxembourg) exercising the statutory licensing and disciplinary oversight under the amended Law of 10 August 1991 on the profession of lawyer and Cabinet Note of 2012.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration on the Roll of the Luxembourg Bar (Tableau de l'Ordre des Avocats) and Certificate of Good Standing (Certificat d'inscription au tableau) as a Qualified Foreign Lawyer or Luxembourg Avocat, authorizing the conduct of cross-border commercial litigation and arbitration from a Luxembourg seat; an exemption from the establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 applies to established regulated legal professions, provided the professional certificate of admission is produced.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) with municipal commune waste authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Exempt from Full EIA and from Preliminary Study: the SCSp executes only office-based legal professional services, generating no industrial discharges, no SEVESO/IEU substances, and no manufacturing footprint; simple notification of office occupancy to the municipal commune suffices
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds set by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 26 July 2017 on waste and the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management: (i) wastewater limited to sanitary municipal sewer loads, pH 6.5-9.5 and BOD below municipal sewer discharge ordinance; (ii) no VOC or solvent emissions other than negligible volatile release from ordinary office cleaning products, below the volatile organic compound threshold under Luxembourg Regulation concerning workplaces; (iii) confidential paper waste must be destroyed under GDPR-compliant secure shredding contracts with certified operators, and all hazardous office waste (toner cartridges, electronics) must be collected by a registered WEEE take-back service per the Law of 20 July 2011 on WEEE

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate and occupancy permit issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) and the municipal Commission de la sécurité after on-site inspection, verifying compliance with the 2021 Regulation on fire prevention in work premises; structural load inspection certificate from a Luxembourg-certified engineer confirming the office floor load-bearing capacity meets IBC-equivalent codes and Grand-Ducal Regulation on public building stability; and occupational health clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering means of evacuation, emergency lighting, first aid provision, and ergonomic workstation compliance

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions and payment services is exercised jointly by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). There is no separate domestic foreign-exchange administration; capital and payment liberalization derives from Articles 63–66 TFEU and Luxembourg financial sector legislation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions. Luxembourg imposes no general exchange controls; profit remittances, partnership distributions to non-resident partners, settlement proceeds, and liquidation distributions are unrestricted. The SCSp is fiscally transparent and Luxembourg levies no withholding tax on its distributions; residual hurdles are limited to standard KYC and source-of-funds validation, CSSF disclosure thresholds, FATCA/CRS reporting, and economic-substance verification for the active litigation business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable within Luxembourg or the euro area: there is no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline for foreign-currency receipts. Foreign-currency receivables (e.g., settlement awards in USD or GBP) may be held in current-account balances or converted at market rates without BCL authorization. If the paying counterparty is located in a jurisdiction with its own surrender regime, that counterparty must satisfy its local central-bank rules before wiring funds to Luxembourg.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Client Trust (IOLTA-style) Account
Escrow (Compte Séquestre) and Current Operational Account
Operational Current Account / Partner Capital Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for a Luxembourg-authorised or EU-passported Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under PSD2; Low for third-country or offshore digital EMIs lacking a Luxembourg branch or passport. Legal constraints: e-money accounts are safeguarded, not bank deposits, and therefore lack Deposit Guarantee Scheme protection; CSSF Circular 20/721 and professional-conduct rules expect lawyers' client monies and pooled IOLTA-style funds to be held in segregated client trust accounts at a credit institution rather than on an EMI float. Recommended allocation: reserve the main IOLTA and escrow clearing functions exclusively for Tier-1 credit institutions and cap EMI usage to minor operational disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate for physical presence if a bank proceeds under an eIDAS-compliant video-identification process and a clean-risk profile; however, Luxembourg banks commonly require an in-person or videoconference interview with the general partner and all UBOs when the SCSp holds pooled litigation funds. Physical attendance in Luxembourg is pragmatically required when: (i) UBOs are resident in high-risk third countries; (ii) the general partner is a corporate manager without local substance; or (iii) source-of-wealth documentation for settlement inflows is incomplete. Recommended defence: appoint a Luxembourg-resident regulated managing partner holding a valid professional licence and pre-clear notarised corporate authorisations, apostilled UBO passports, and a CSSF-compliant CDD file before the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification failure for the SCSp (Luxembourg RBE beneficial-ownership register filing)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership deed (acte de constitution), RBE filing receipt, certified UBO diagram, proof of the general partner's regulatory status, and passport copies of all natural persons holding 25% or more interest or control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds or source-of-wealth challenge on litigation settlement and escrow proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Retainer and engagement letters, court judgments or arbitration awards, settlement agreements, invoice ledger, full bank-statement chain tracing the origin of funds, originating-jurisdiction tax clearance, and a sworn source-of-wealth declaration from the paying party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or sanctions exposure in cross-border commercial litigation (CSSF Regulation 12-02 and EU AML framework)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UN/EU/OFAC sanctions-screening results for all parties, independent counsel legal opinion confirming the bona fide proceedings, no-sanctions-nexus certificate, PEP disclosure with an enhanced-monitoring plan, and a litigation-case summary with docket references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance and pass-through-vehicle screening of the SCSp
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg registered-office certificate, local general partner or manager appointment, partner and board minutes evidencing real decision-making, staffing and payroll evidence, professional-indemnity (RC professionnelle) certificate, Luxembourg VAT and tax return filings, and annual accounts for the litigation chambers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory licensing verification for legal-services activity (ISIC 6910)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Ordre des Avocats admission-roll extract for responsible counsel, any Ministry of Justice or Bar-authorised alternative business structure licence, professional-liability insurance policy, and jurisdictional registration certificates for all foreign affiliated counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route partner capital injections and client settlement inflows via SWIFT MT103 with a compliant purpose-code architecture: classify partner contributions under the direct-investment category of the ECB balance-of-payments reporting, and litigation fees or settlement proceeds under the legal-services service category. Reference the SCSp's Luxembourg IBAN in field 57A, include an explicit purpose memo in field 70, and upload the underlying contract or court order into the bank's documentation workflow. EUR-denominated transfers may clear via SEPA Credit Transfer; non-EUR currencies settle through correspondent banking. Credit is deferred until sanctions screening and counterparty KYC are clean, and cash received from unrepresented third parties may be rejected under client-money rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for counsel fees, expert witnesses, court registries, enforcement agents, and adverse-cost awards clear via: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers; (ii) SWIFT MT202 or MT202 COV for correspondent-leg cover; (iii) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for urgent intra-EUR payments; and (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit or escrow-release protocols for staged settlement payoffs against court orders. Each instruction must be signed by the general partner, pre-screened for sanctions, and supported by an invoice, court order, or settlement memorandum. Records are retained under CSSF CDD rules for a minimum of five years after the business relationship ends, extended to ten years where enhanced due diligence applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX Forwards (EUR versus USD, GBP, and CHF) for scheduled settlement conversions
Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-fully-convertible emerging-market currencies tied to litigation recoveries
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for matching multi-currency settlement liabilities and receipts
Vanilla FX Options used solely as commercial cover for contingent award conversion risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) of the SCSp approved by the partners and filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the partners within six months after financial year-end; filing within one month of approval, resulting in a hard deadline of seven months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative notice and late-filing fine of up to EUR 10,000; persistent failure for two consecutive years exposes the general partner and management to judicial dissolution and de-registration (strike-off) proceedings at the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership dataset in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 15 October; confirmation certifies the RBE data as at 30 September of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late confirmation triggers an administrative warning, followed by recurring daily fines up to EUR 250 per day and, after several defaults, criminal sanctions and judicial dissolution of the SCSp for non-compliance with AML framework

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax declaration and supporting statements filed with the direct tax administration for the fiscally transparent SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg direct tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year accounts; a three-month extension to 15 March is available on timely request to the ACD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax, monthly interest of 0.80%, ex officio assessment by the tax inspector, and joint and several liability of the general partner for under-declared items

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax (IFF) declaration for the SCSp and its corporate general partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration and payment due by 31 December of the year following the relevant tax year, or within three months of the financial year-end for non-calendar year SCSp accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at 0.80% per month, plus a 10% late-payment surcharge and automatic reassessment; the corporate general partner remains liable for the SCSp's net wealth tax exposure

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé applies if the SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds at balance-sheet date for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average headcount above 50; audit is also compulsory where the SCSp qualifies as a regulated alternative investment fund or where the general partner is a corporate group required to produce consolidated audited accounts
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, as amended) or, at the partners' option, IFRS as endorsed by the European Union; small SCSp may file an abbreviated balance sheet using the LBR XBRL taxonomy

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an internal beneficial-owner register and mirror filings in the Luxembourg RBE; each transfer of partnership interests, any change in the special partner or general partner, and any evolution of ultimate beneficial ownership must be declared to the RBE within one month of the event, and the complete dataset must be positively confirmed annually no later than 15 October; the confirmation recertifies existing data and does not replace a fresh registration
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (SCSp special and general partners)
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests
Register of Beneficial Owners (internal RBE file)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – 5,400 per annum (EUR 1,600 – 5,000), reflecting the Luxembourg corporate-agent market for registered office, RCS correspondence, and compliance liaison
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – 28,000 per certified audit engagement (EUR 5,500 – 25,000) depending on transaction volume, number of partners, and cross-border litigation activity; no audit fee is incurred if the SCSp falls below the statutory thresholds and is not an AIF

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is fiscally transparent: no CIT, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at the entity level; income and gains are allocated to its partners. Corporate partners resident in Luxembourg may benefit from the 80% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, the 80% IP box exemption on net qualifying IP income, and full relief under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where applicable. Individuals are taxed at progressive rates after the 50% diversification abatement for qualifying Luxembourg-source dividends, subject to standard progressive tax bands.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration fiscale d'une société de personnes) filed electronically through the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal 'MyGuichet.lu' (professional space); corporate partners also attach Form 500 (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) where required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by 30 June of the following year; electronic filing automatically extends the filing deadline to 31 July. The Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) may grant further extension upon written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal name, RCS registration number, registered office, and LEI code of the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg RCS number; for non-resident corporate partners, identify them in the partner schedule and do not apply Luxembourg CIT to their allocable income unless they operate a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and fiscal year-end declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the date matches the partnership agreement and the last approved annual accounts; non-resident partners may have different tax year-ends for their domestic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocated taxable income or loss to each corporate partner, including any Luxembourg permanent establishment share.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show only the portion taxable in Luxembourg; attach proof of tax residence (TRC) of the foreign corporate partner and compute the allocation strictly per the partnership deed and arm's-length principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocated taxable income or loss to each individual/contractual partner, for Luxembourg personal income tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident individuals report only Luxembourg-source income in their domestic returns; Luxembourg will assess only in case of a Luxembourg permanent establishment or a domestic business register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income, royalties, capital gains and other receipts generated in connection with litigation, asset tracing, and dispute financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include worldwide litigation fees earned by a non-resident partner unless the activity is attributable to the SCSp's Luxembourg commercial establishment; follow the treaty PE rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distribution made or deemed distribution to partners, if any, for purposes of verifying that no Luxembourg WHT applies on partnership distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that distributions to non-resident partners are exempt from Luxembourg WHT because the SCSp is a transparent partnership; no claim is required beyond the filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit relief and allocable tax withheld by third countries where the litigation or tracing activity produced foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion the foreign tax credit to each partner pro-rata; a non-resident partner typically cannot use the Luxembourg credit if the income is not effectively taxed in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intercompany transactions and transfer pricing documentation flag for the SCSp's intra-group dealings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare every controlled transaction with non-resident related parties above EUR 100,000 (services/financial) or EUR 500,000 (goods) and attach the supporting Local/Master File references.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual partnership return triggers a fixed administrative penalty of EUR 150 plus an additional surcharge of 10% on the assessed tax if filed after an official reminder. Late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% annually). Deliberate non-filing or false filing constitutes tax fraud and is punishable by a fine up to EUR 250,000, imprisonment of up to 5 years, and an assessment penalty of 100% of the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard dividend withholding tax on dividends distributed by Luxembourg corporations; 0% on distributions by the SCSp because it is fiscally transparent. Qualifying corporate partners resident in the EU/EEA or in a treaty country may obtain full exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0%) and Luxembourg's participation exemption regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced or zero withholding under an income tax treaty: (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from the residence jurisdiction; (2) file the required reduced-rate/exemption certificate with the Luxembourg withholding agent or directly with the ACD using the official forms (and, for EU residents, a statement under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive); (3) if tax was withheld at source, apply for a refund through the Luxembourg 'Form 800' procedure within three years of the withholding date, attaching the original TRC, the SCSp's transparency ruling if any, and the underlying distribution documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic withholding tax under Luxembourg law on arm's-length royalties paid to non-residents, with treaty rates generally 0-5%; interest: 0% statutory WHT on arm's-length interest paid to non-residents (except profit-sharing loans or excess interest), subject to treaty rates of 0-10% if the domestic exemption is not available. Both rates are effectively nil for most OECD/EU counterparties, provided the beneficiary is the beneficial owner and the transactions have economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 (group consolidated revenue) for CbC Report and Master File; Luxembourg Local File is required when intra-group controlled transactions exceed EUR 500,000 per goods/services category or EUR 100,000 for financial transactions and management fees, per Article 56bis LIR and the Luxembourg TP Circular.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not enact UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but it applies the ATAD GAAR, CFC rules, and judicial doctrines (abus de droit, substance-over-form) requiring genuine business purpose and real economic substance for treaty and EU directive benefits. Administrative circulars (notably LIR.S.234-1) require evidence of local decision-making, local employees, office premises, independent commercial risk control, and practical management for an SCSp to obtain a tax residency certificate or benefit from the participation exemption and DTA relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a nil return while distributing profits to undisclosed partners, omitting allocable litigation income or asset-tracing fees, or concealing the existence of the SCSp's Luxembourg commercial activity from the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at up to 100% of the tax evaded, payment of late interest at 0.6% per month, criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000, imprisonment for up to 5 years, publication of the judgment in the press and prohibition from practicing as a managing partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners found personally complicit may be jointly and severally liable for the SCSp's tax debt, face asset seizure, travel bans and administrative immobilisation through the Luxembourg tax collection procedure (avis à tiers détenteur), plus disqualification from administering legal entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or operating the SCSp as a pure mailbox with no employees, no board meetings or no local decision-making, using it exclusively to channel legal fees, dividends or interest commissions to low-tax jurisdictions overnight, and denying all substance to the Luxembourg tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may disregard the arrangement and re-characterise it as a taxable Luxembourg company; a 25% administrative surcharge on the under-assessed tax, late interest at 0.6% per month, and denial of treaty and Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits with retroactive effect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and managers who knowingly structure a shell may incur civil liability for the re-characterised profits, be subject to personal tax assessments under the CFC/anti-abuse rules, and, where cross-border tax fraud is proven, face extradition, travel bans and penal sanctions under the Luxembourg Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep contemporaneous Local File and Master File; refusing to disclose benchmark studies to the ACD; applying a gross margin below the Luxembourg interquartile range; or concluding a high-volume services agreement with a related offshore service company without supporting substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may make a unilateral re-assessment using the arm's-length margin it determines, add late interest at 0.6% per month and impose a 25% negligence penalty (50% if bad faith); repeated non-cooperation may trigger criminal administrative sanctions of up to EUR 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false TP certificates or who instruct accountants to manipulate transactional data may be held personally liable for the gross-up penalties and face criminal conviction for aiding tax evasion; the Luxembourg commercial register may impose a temporary ban against running a business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Effective Beneficial Owners (REBEC); using bearer shares or trusts without disclosing the settlor and beneficiary; or processing litigation proceeds through an IOLTA trust account without performing KYC/AML checks on the non-resident partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 1,250,000 for the legal entity; imprisonment of up to 5 years for responsible individuals; corrective order to file the UBO declaration with a per-violation fine of EUR 15,000; possible freezing of the SCSp's bank accounts under the 2004 AML Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and professional partners are personally exposed to money-laundering liability under Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq., including confiscation of assets, travel bans, prohibition from professional practice, and extradition if the predicate offence occurred abroad; the Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission may publish a formal sanction against the individual.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeatedly missing Form 510 filing deadlines, failing to pay municipal business tax advances, or refusing to answer demarches from the ACD regarding the partner allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed EUR 150 late-filing penalty, automatic 10% surcharge on taxes due, default interest at 0.6% per month, and estimated assessment by the ACD which is immediately collectable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Although not criminal per se, a general partner who is a director signatory of the SCSp's registration documents may be held civilly liable for the estimated tax if the partnership has insufficient assets, and a deliberate pattern of non-filing may lead to a travel ban under the Luxembourg General Tax Code enforcement measures.
